_about: Compliance rules for the SonicWall EXP audit. Edit these values to match client policy; sonicwall_compare.py reads this file at runtime.
_trusted_zone_note: The main internal / trusted network. All inter-VLAN access is judged relative to this zone.
_trusted_zones_note: Zones treated as trusted user networks alongside the LAN. SSL VPN remote users land in SSLVPN and legitimately need to reach LAN servers/resources, so SSLVPN->LAN is allowed and NOT flagged. Any zone NOT in this list that reaches the LAN is a red flag. Management access is governed separately by management.admin_allowed_zones (LAN only) — being a trusted DATA zone does not grant firewall-management access.
_vpn_user_zones_note: Zones holding remote-access VPN USERS. Two rules apply: (1) VPN user-to-user traffic must be blocked (intra-zone communication off) to stop lateral movement between remote sessions; (2) the LAN must NOT initiate connections TO these zones (LAN->SSLVPN blocked) — remote users reach LAN servers, not the other way around.

lan_requirements._note: Content filtering and IPS/IDS are REQUIRED on the trusted LAN. Any VLAN/zone/interface allowed to talk INTO the LAN is a red flag.

ssh._note: SSH management must be enabled, may ONLY be reachable from the LAN zone, and must be restricted to at most 2 source IPs.

management.admin_source_description: the jumpbox that runs the Connect Secure agent
management._external_mgmt_note: Management rules whose Source is this address object/group are the sanctioned external (datacenter) management path — KEEP them; they are not flagged as off-zone. If the object still carries a legacy name (e.g. the SonicWall default 'GMS Addresses' group), the fix is to RENAME it to external_mgmt_source, not to delete the rule.
management._note: The admin interface (HTTPS/HTTP/SNMP) and SSH may ONLY be reachable from the LAN zone, and must be IP-restricted to at most max_source_ips. Every other zone — VPN, WAN, and all other VLANs — must be denied management access. To also permit IP-restricted WAN/GMS management, add "WAN" to admin_allowed_zones. Unrestricted (Any-source) management access is a red flag.

nsm._note: The fleet is managed centrally by NSM from the RT Datacenter. Each firewall must have the GMS/NSM management channel enabled (gmsServerEnable=on) AND a management access rule whose Source is management.external_mgmt_source (or one of its legacy names). Set required to false to skip this rule.

vpn._mfa_note: Any of accepted_mfa satisfies the SSL VPN MFA rule: DUO (named in the config), Entra (SAML), TOTP / Email OTP (SonicOS one-time passwords on the VPN user group). A RADIUS login server is only counted as MFA if its IP is listed in mfa_radius_servers (e.g. the DUO Authentication Proxy); otherwise RADIUS login yields WARN 'verify', never a FAIL.
vpn._note: If SSL VPN is configured, DUO or Entra (SAML) MFA is REQUIRED. Directory should be AD/LDAP or Entra.

external_services._note: WAN-inbound services open to any source are red flags, except expected VPN listeners which must accept any remote IP.

consistency._note: Across all firewalls for one client, geo-blocking and blocked content-filter categories must match. If one firewall blocks something, they all must. The STRICTEST firewall (union of everything blocked) is the baseline; anything missing on a peer is an exception.

_expected_vlan_roles_note: Suggested VLAN plan the audit checks every firewall against. Each entry: vlan (suggested ID, null = no suggested ID), role, purpose, match (case-insensitive substrings looked for in the VLAN sub-interface name + comment), optional exclude (substrings that disqualify a match), segmentation (recommended access policy shown in the reports). A configured VLAN that matches no role is listed for naming/classification; an unnamed VLAN whose ID equals a suggested ID is hinted to that role.

expected_vlan_roles.segmentation: Most restricted. Permit only from admin/jump box; deny from User, Guest, IoT. No inbound internet; outbound to vendor update sources only.
Allow only required ports from User VLAN. No inbound from Guest/IoT. No direct inbound internet; publish externally via reverse proxy / DMZ.
Internet allowed. Reach Servers on required ports only. Deny lateral access to Mgmt, CCTV, and IoT.
Isolate with QoS. Permit only SIP/RTP to PBX/provider. No general internet; deny access to data VLANs.
Allow print/scan from User VLAN only. Block internet (allow vendor cloud-print if required). Deny inbound from Guest/IoT.
Treat as trusted user VLAN. 802.1X or strong PSK. Same server access policy as wired users.
Internet-only. Enable client isolation. Password protected. Deny all access to internal VLANs.

expected_vlan_roles.purpose: Smart devices, thermostats, BYOD (incl. HVAC, postage meters)
expected_vlan_roles.segmentation: Isolate from corporate. Internet limited to required cloud endpoints. Deny access to Servers, Mgmt, Workstations.
Isolate NVR and cameras. No internet (or vendor-only). Management access from Mgmt/admin VLAN only.
Strict firewall both directions. Deny initiation into internal VLANs; internal reaches DMZ on required ports only.
Isolate; permit only the ATM-to-processor traffic. Deny access to all other VLANs.
Permit only the core-banking application ports from Servers/Users. Deny from Guest, IoT and Wi-Fi.

expected_vlan_roles.purpose: Federal Reserve FedLine router (bank-specific, no suggested ID)
expected_vlan_roles.segmentation: Isolate; permit only the designated FedLine workstation(s). No other VLAN access.
